name: Wilkinson’s trial cylinder
summary: A roughly 18-inch engine cylinder machined by ironmaster John Wilkinson to replace the cylinder of Watt's experimental steam engine at Soho.
description: An approximately 18-inch replacement cylinder machined by John Wilkinson and supplied for Watt's experimental engine at Soho.
tier_reason: Fine historical detail or an evidentiary witness; retention supports explanation without claiming broad later dependence.
why: Watt's engine needed a replacement cylinder true enough to keep steam from leaking past the piston.

date.label: by 24 April 1775 or 1776; letter year disputed
date.basis: Andrew dates the supply letter to April 1775 and Muirhead’s 1854 contents dates it 24 April 1775, but the heading of the reproduced letter itself prints 24 April 1776. Conservatively the claimed supply is bounded by the later printed date until the manuscript is inspected; no earliest production date is established.

events.statement: An approximately 18-inch replacement cylinder machined by John Wilkinson and supplied for Watt's experimental engine at Soho.
events.caveats: The actual machine used for this small cylinder is not securely identified. Andrew proposes a rotating-workpiece cannon-boring machine as a likelihood; that conjecture is not adopted as fact. The 1854 edition has conflicting 1775 and 1776 letter dates; Andrew follows 1775. The original manuscript has not been inspected, so a suspected printing error is not resolved here.

evidence.supports: Replacement cylinder, correspondence dates, Wilkinson supply and Soho trial context.

evidence.locator: Contents p. x (letter 146); letter 146 heading and body printed p. 84
evidence.supports: Contents prints 24 April 1775 while the actual letter heading prints 24 April 1776; the body reports the replacement cylinder.

events.statement: Muirhead’s published letter disclosed the supplied cylinder; Andrew attributes the supply to Wilkinson.
events.scope: The approximately 18-inch replacement cylinder supplied for Watt’s experimental Soho engine.
events.caveats: No sale or earlier public disclosure of this exact small cylinder was established. The published heading prints 1776, the contents print 1775, and the underlying original letter was not examined.
